description: §5.2.3's named-function worked example — two-statement intent lifted to a named function and wired by name (`onclick=startGame()`) does NOT fire E-MULTI-STATEMENT-HANDLER. The `;` separators live inside the function body, an expression-internal context.
rationale: §5.2.3 (amended S435): "The inline block and a named function are a free choice. `function startOver() { … }` wired as `onclick=startOver()` remains fully valid". The handler value is exactly one expression — the bare-call shape §5.2.3's table admits — so the code SHALL stay silent. This is the NEG mirror of `multi-stmt-handler-attr-pos`. It also pins the scanner's expression-internal-context qualifier: the two `;` in the function body must NOT count as top-level hits.
